messages.text: Mowbray steps down from Blackburn due to health issues

metadata.summary: Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues.
metadata.content: Tony Mowbray steps down as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tony Mowbray steps down as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues Tuesday 17 November 2026 11:14, UK Image: Tony Mowbray has left Blackburn Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues. The 62-year-old returned to football at West Brom last year following his recovery from bowel cancer, before taking charge at Blackburn in June. In a statement, Mowbray said: "Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers. "I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them. "Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you've given me. It's been a pleasure working alongside you. "To the fans, thank you for the way you've supported me and the team this season. I've always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me. "I'm grateful to the owners and Suhail [Shaikh, Blackburn's chief operating officer] for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again. "I'd ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. "Thank you for your understanding. Tony." Mowbray had enjoyed an impressive start to his second spell at Blackburn. messages.text: Cox: Three hundreds not enough to keep Buttler out

metadata.summary: Jordan Cox insists Jos Buttler has earned the right to come back into England's ODI side, even if he was to score three hundreds while the country's "best ever" white-ball player recovers from injury.
metadata.content: Jordan Cox: Three hundreds not enough to keep Jos Buttler out - 'England's best ever' | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jordan Cox: Three hundreds not enough to keep Jos Buttler out - 'England's best ever' England's Jordan Cox ahead of series-deciding third ODI vs Australia quips scoring three hundreds would not be enough to keep Jos Buttler out of the side when latter returns, hailing him 'England's best ever' Tuesday 17 November 2026 11:42, UK Image: England's Jordan Cox hopes to play a pivotal role in the ODI series decider against Australia in Hobart on Wednesday Jordan Cox insists Jos Buttler has earned the right to come back into England's ODI side, even if he was to score three hundreds while the country's "best ever" white-ball player recovers from injury. Cox will continue to bat and keep wicket in the ODI series decider against Australia at Hobart's Bellerive Oval on Wednesday, having scored a lively 67 in England's series-levelling win in Adelaide last time out. He owes his place in the XI to Buttler's torn hamstring and is pragmatic when it comes to his prospects of keeping the shirt for next year's World Cup campaign. Asked about his chances of winning that particular selection battle, he said: "I don't think so, no. I think what Jos has done for English cricket in general [is too much]. messages.text: 'I didn't want to look back on my career with regret' - the journey of Aaron Connolly

metadata.summary: It is easy to forget that Aaron Connolly is still only 26, considering everything he has already experienced.
metadata.content: Aaron Connolly: Leyton Orient forward reflects on eventful career path from Premier League full debut goals for Brighton to set backs and comebacks | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Aaron Connolly: Leyton Orient forward reflects on eventful career path from Premier League full debut goals for Brighton to set backs and comebacks Aaron Connolly speaks to Sky Sports about his breakthrough at Brighton and the pitfalls and setbacks that followed on his journey in the game. He is now rebuilding in League One at Leyton Orient and determined to forge a career he can be proud of. Simeon Gholam EFL Editor @simeongholam Tuesday 17 November 2026 11:52, UK It is easy to forget that Aaron Connolly is still only 26, considering everything he has already experienced. Just over seven years have passed since that magical full Premier League debut, scoring twice for Brighton against Spurs at the age of 19 in 2019. In the time since, there have been injuries that have damaged his progress in football and obstacles in his life beyond the pitch. "It's been tough," Connolly - now at Leyton Orient - tells Sky Sports . "It's probably been well documented that I haven't dealt with setbacks very well before. "I love playing football. It's what I've done my whole life. So when I can't, it's obviously difficult. "I've had a spell of injuries and interruptions.
